newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds edge up as Congress musters quorum.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds edge up as Congress musters quorum.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished slightly higher Wednesday after Congress mustered quorum to debate the government's tax-hiking measures in the afternoon.
Although the quorum lent some support, traders said the market settled into a period of calm Wednesday after a sharp rally Friday and Monday followed by profit-taking Tuesday.

"I think the market is likely to be very quiet until the FOMC meeting next week," said an analyst at a large Argentine bank. The U.S. Federal Open Market Committee meets next Tuesday to set the direction of U.S. interest rates.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.05 to 117.85, while Argentina's FRB due 2005 was up 1/8 at 82-3/4.
On Tuesday, the Bocon Pre 2 plunged $0.80 and the FRB fell 1-1/8.
Traders said market activity was thin.

Domestic market players said the decision by the U.S. FOMC on interest rates next week will be key for the market's performance because it will have a large impact on the current global high liquidity levels said to be supporting emerging markets.
"The international climate for the market is favorable," said the analyst.
In the money markets, one-day call money rates fell to 6.45 percent from 6.63 percent.
